questions.question: The formula for concentration, read as a sentence, is:
options: Concentration equals the moles of solute divided by the volume of solution in dm³
Concentration equals the mass divided by the molar mass
Concentration equals the volume divided by the moles
Concentration equals the grams dissolved per litre, no conversion needed

questions.question: 500 cm³ of solution, expressed in the units the formula c = n/V requires, is:
options: 500 dm³
5 dm³
0,5 dm³
0,05 dm³

questions.question: 8 g of NaOH (M = 40 g/mol) in 0,5 dm³ of solution gives a concentration of:
options: 16 mol·dm⁻³
0,4 mol·dm⁻³
0,1 mol·dm⁻³
4 mol·dm⁻³

questions.question: Why must the 8 g of NaOH become 0,2 mol before dividing by the volume?
options: Because grams are too small to divide
Because the volume is also in grams
Because moles make the number bigger
Because concentration counts dissolved particles in moles, not their mass in grams

subtopics.title: Percentage Composition — the Compound's Mass Recipe

questions.question: The percentage by mass of an element in a compound equals:
options: The number of atoms of that element times 100
The atomic mass of the element divided by 100
The mass of that element in one mole of compound, divided by the molar mass, times 100
The molar mass divided by the element's mass, times 100

questions.question: In water, H₂O (M = 18 g/mol), the percentage of hydrogen by mass is:
In CO₂, the oxygen contributes 32 g per mole and not 16 g because:
options: Oxygen is heavier in gases
The subscript 2 means two oxygen atoms are counted
Carbon donates mass to oxygen
The 16 must be doubled only at STP

questions.question: A learner's percentages for a compound total 92%. This means:
options: The remaining 8% is always water
The compound is 92% pure
Nothing — totals below 100% are normal
An arithmetic error was made — the elements' percentages must total 100%

subtopics.title: Empirical Formula — the Recipe Recovered from Percentages

questions.question: Assuming a 100 g sample when given percentages is allowed because:
options: A ratio is unchanged by sample size, and 100 g turns each percentage directly into a mass
All laboratory samples weigh 100 g
Percentages only work for exactly 100 g
It rounds the answer to whole numbers

questions.question: For 40,0% C, 6,7% H, 53,3% O, the mole values before simplifying are:
After dividing each mole value by the smallest, the ratio C : H : O = 1 : 2 : 1 gives the empirical formula:
options: C₂HO
CH₂O
C₂H₄O₂
CHO₂

questions.question: If dividing by the smallest leaves a ratio of 1 : 1,5, the correct move is:
options: Round 1,5 down to 1
Round 1,5 up to 2
Start the calculation again
Multiply both numbers by 2 to get 2 : 3

subtopics.title: Water of Crystallisation, the Full Method and the Traps

questions.question: In CuSO₄·5H₂O, the '5H₂O' means:
options: The crystals are dissolved in five litres of water
Five water molecules are locked into the crystal with every CuSO₄ unit
The compound is 5% water
Water must be added five times during preparation

questions.question: Using M(CuSO₄) = 159,5 g/mol and 5 × 18 = 90 g of water, the percentage of water in CuSO₄·5H₂O is:
A concentration calculated with the volume left in cm³ instead of dm³ comes out:
options: One thousand times too small
One thousand times too big
Ten times too small
Unchanged — the units cancel

questions.question: Why can mass percentages never be read directly as atom ratios?
options: Percentages are always rounded
Mass ratios only work for gases
The laboratory cannot measure mass accurately
Atoms have different masses, so equal masses contain different numbers of atoms — only moles count atoms

questions.question: In the cooldrink picture, a 'strong' solution is one with:
options: A bigger jug
More total liquid
More moles of solute packed into each cubic decimetre
A higher temperature

questions.question: One mole of NaOH weighs 40 g because:
options: Sodium 23 plus oxygen 16 plus hydrogen 1 add to 40
All bases weigh 40 g per mole
40 is the atomic number of NaOH
The balance rounds to the nearest ten

questions.question: Two jugs hold the same total dissolved substance, but jug B is twice the volume of jug A. Then:
options: Both jugs have the same concentration
Jug B has twice the concentration of jug A
The concentrations cannot be compared
Jug B has half the concentration of jug A

questions.question: The answer 0,4 mol·dm⁻³ means, in plain words:
options: The solution weighs 0,4 grams per litre
Every full litre of this solution holds 0,4 moles of dissolved NaOH
The jug is 0,4 litres in size
0,4% of the solution is NaOH

questions.question: The empirical formula problem is like reading a recipe backwards because:
options: You start from the finished compound's percentages and recover the atom ratio
You must cook the compound first
The formula is written right to left
Percentages are always written in reverse order

questions.question: Masses are converted to moles before simplifying the ratio because:
options: Moles are easier to divide
Grams cannot be written in a formula
A formula counts atoms, and moles count atoms while grams weigh them
The calculator requires moles

questions.question: The simplifying step of the method is: divide every mole value by:
options: One hundred
The largest mole value
The molar mass
The smallest mole value

questions.question: For the compound with C : H : O moles of 3,33 : 6,7 : 3,33, the empirical formula is:
options: C₃H₆O₃
CH₂O
C₂HO₂
CHO

subtopics.title: The Water Hiding in Dry Crystals

questions.question: When blue copper sulfate crystals are heated gently:
options: They melt into a blue liquid
They turn white, lose mass, and give off their water of crystallisation
They gain mass from the air
Nothing happens because they are dry

questions.question: The molar mass of the whole crystal CuSO₄·5H₂O used in the calculation is:
options: 159,5 g/mol
90 g/mol
177,5 g/mol
249,5 g/mol

questions.question: The mass lost on heating agrees with the calculated 36,1%. This agreement shows that:
options: A formula makes a prediction that a laboratory balance can confirm
The balance was faulty
Water always makes up a third of any crystal
Heating creates new mass

questions.question: The two habits that protect every calculation in this lesson are:
options: Round early, and ignore small subscripts
Moles before anything, and treat every subscript as a multiplication instruction
Always assume STP, and work in kilograms
Memorise all formulas, and skip the sense-check
